This Change Request is raised to cover the replacement of the exhaust silencer unit and the two (2) flexible bellows on generator set G-7 (Caterpillar G3516, unit serial EK-G7-118) located at the Eket Gas Plant compressor station.

During the routine vibration monitoring carried out on 16 July 2021, readings on the exhaust stack of G-7 indicated a progressive increase in vibration amplitude, specifically at the horizontal plane of the silencer mounting brackets. A subsequent visual inspection on 19 July 2021 revealed the following:

a) Cracking of the outer shell of the exhaust silencer, approximately 300 mm from the top mounting lug, running circumferentially for roughly 40% of the shell circumference.
b) Deterioration and flattening of the flexible bellows connecting the turbocharger outlet to the silencer inlet. The bellows show signs of metal fatigue and partial collapse, likely accelerated by repeated thermal cycling and the presence of corrosive elements in the exhaust gas.
c) Evidence of exhaust gas leakage at the bellows flanges, indicated by soot staining.

The above defects constitute a safety hazard and a risk to the integrity of the exhaust system. Continued operation without rectification could lead to catastrophic failure of the silencer, potentially causing damage to the turbocharger, exhaust ducting, and adjacent equipment, and posing a risk to personnel.

4. REASON FOR CHANGE

The change is required to restore the generator set to a safe and reliable operating condition. The current silencer and bellows have been in service since the original plant commissioning in 2014 and have exceeded their expected service life of approximately 20,000 operating hours. The generator set has accumulated approximately 24,500 operating hours to date.

Change Request CR-2021-014 status approved status. Record status: historical.

The replacement is considered a corrective maintenance activity under the scope of the existing maintenance contract. However, due to the specialised nature of the exhaust silencer and the need for a specific replacement part (not a standard inventory item), it is necessary to raise this Change Request to cover the procurement of the new silencer and bellows, as these are not included in the current spares inventory or the annual maintenance budget.

5. SCOPE OF WORK

The following work is required to complete this change:

a) Procurement of one (1) replacement exhaust silencer for G-7, model to match original specifications (refer to attached technical datasheet, Appendix A).
b) Procurement of two (2) flexible bellows assemblies, complete with flanges and gaskets (refer to Appendix B).
c) Isolation of generator G-7 and issuance of a valid Work Permit for Safe Work (hot work permit required for cutting and welding).
d) Removal of the existing silencer and flexible bellows. This will require the use of a mobile crane (50-tonne capacity) to lift the silencer, which weighs approximately 1,200 kg.
e) Installation of the new silencer and flexible bellows, including alignment and torqueing of flange bolts to specification.
f) Non-destructive testing (NDT) of the new welds (dye penetrant test on the silencer support bracket welds).
g) Re-commissioning of the generator set, including a 4-hour load bank test to verify exhaust system integrity and vibration levels.
h) Disposal of removed parts as per site waste management procedures.

6. COST IMPACT

The estimated cost for this change is broken down as follows:
All costs are exclusive of VAT. VAT at the prevailing rate (7.5%) will be charged separately and
shown on the corresponding invoice.

7. SCHEDULE IMPACT

The required parts have a lead time of approximately 6–8 weeks from date of order confirmation.
Delivery will be to the Port of Lagos, followed by customs clearance and road transport to site
(approximately 5–7 working days). We therefore propose the following indicative schedule:

| Activity | Estimated Duration | Proposed Dates |
|----------|--------------------|----------------|
| Purchase order placement | – | 05/08/2021 |
| Manufacturing & delivery to Lagos | 6–8 weeks | Mid-September 2021 |
| Customs clearance & transport to site | 5–7 working days | Late September 2021 |
| Installation (incl. crane, NDT, recommissioning) | 5 working days | Early October 2021 |

Total estimated schedule impact: **no impact on the overall maintenance outage window**, provided
the purchase order is raised by the date indicated above. If procurement is delayed beyond
15/08/2021, the installation will need to be deferred to the next planned maintenance window
(January 2022), as the generator cannot be taken offline outside the agreed outage schedule without
affecting plant availability guarantees.

8. JUSTIFICATION

The exhaust silencer on G-7 has developed visible corrosion and thinning at the lower shell section,
particularly around the drain point. Acoustic measurements taken on 12/07/2021 recorded a noise
level of 98 dB(A) at 1 metre from the silencer, against a design limit of 85 dB(A). The flexible
bellows show signs of fatigue cracking at the convolutions. Continued operation carries a risk of
exhaust leak, noise exceedance, and potential damage to the turbocharger outlet flange if the
bellows fail completely. Replacement is therefore recommended at the earliest opportunity.

Following the approval recorded in Section 9 above, the site maintenance team has reviewed the
proposed installation window against the current plant outage schedule. The originally indicated
window in Section 5 (dated 20/07/2021) is no longer fully available due to a delay in the
completion of the GT-2 combustion inspection, which has pushed the next planned outage start by

**13. CLARIFICATION – NOISE MEASUREMENT METHOD**

During the pre-approval technical review, a question was raised regarding the noise measurement
method used to identify the exhaust noise exceedance. For the avoidance of doubt, the measurement
referred to in Section 8 was taken in accordance with the plant's standard condition monitoring
procedure (CMP-012), using a handheld sound level meter set to 'A' weighting, slow response, at a
distance of 1 metre from the silencer casing, with the unit operating at base load. The measured
level was 93 dB(A), which exceeds the design limit of 85 dB(A). No further measurements have been
taken since the date of the original inspection. The replacement silencer specified in Appendix A
is expected to restore noise levels to within the design limit.

**14. CLARIFICATION – BELLOWS CONDITION AND REPLACEMENT SCOPE**

The flexible bellows assemblies identified in Section 5 are the inlet and outlet connections to
the exhaust silencer. The fatigue cracking observed at the convolutions is limited to the outlet
bellows; however, due to the common age and service history of both assemblies, and to avoid a
repeat outage in the near term, the scope includes replacement of both inlet and outlet bellows.

documents.title: Change Request CR-2021-014
documents.content:
This Change Request is raised to cover the replacement of the exhaust silencer unit and the two (2) flexible bellows on generator set G-7 (Caterpillar G3516, unit serial EK-G7-118) located at the Eket Gas Plant compressor station.

During the routine vibration monitoring carried out on 16 July 2021, readings on the exhaust stack of G-7 indicated a progressive increase in vibration amplitude, specifically at the horizontal plane of the silencer mounting brackets. A subsequent visual inspection on 19 July 2021 revealed the following:

a) Cracking of the outer shell of the exhaust silencer, approximately 300 mm from the top mounting lug, running circumferentially for roughly 40% of the shell circumference.
b) Deterioration and flattening of the flexible bellows connecting the turbocharger outlet to the silencer inlet. The bellows show signs of metal fatigue and partial collapse, likely accelerated by repeated thermal cycling and the presence of corrosive elements in the exhaust gas.
c) Evidence of exhaust gas leakage at the bellows flanges, indicated by soot staining.

The above defects constitute a safety hazard and a risk to the integrity of the exhaust system. Continued operation without rectification could lead to catastrophic failure of the silencer, potentially causing damage to the turbocharger, exhaust ducting, and adjacent equipment, and posing a risk to personnel.

4. REASON FOR CHANGE

The change is required to restore the generator set to a safe and reliable operating condition. The current silencer and bellows have been in service since the original plant commissioning in 2014 and have exceeded their expected service life of approximately 20,000 operating hours. The generator set has accumulated approximately 24,500 operating hours to date.

Change Request CR-2021-014 status approved status. Record status: historical.

The replacement is considered a corrective maintenance activity under the scope of the existing maintenance contract. However, due to the specialised nature of the exhaust silencer and the need for a specific replacement part (not a standard inventory item), it is necessary to raise this Change Request to cover the procurement of the new silencer and bellows, as these are not included in the current spares inventory or the annual maintenance budget.

5. SCOPE OF WORK

The following work is required to complete this change:

a) Procurement of one (1) replacement exhaust silencer for G-7, model to match original specifications (refer to attached technical datasheet, Appendix A).
b) Procurement of two (2) flexible bellows assemblies, complete with flanges and gaskets (refer to Appendix B).
c) Isolation of generator G-7 and issuance of a valid Work Permit for Safe Work (hot work permit required for cutting and welding).
d) Removal of the existing silencer and flexible bellows. This will require the use of a mobile crane (50-tonne capacity) to lift the silencer, which weighs approximately 1,200 kg.
e) Installation of the new silencer and flexible bellows, including alignment and torqueing of flange bolts to specification.
f) Non-destructive testing (NDT) of the new welds (dye penetrant test on the silencer support bracket welds).
g) Re-commissioning of the generator set, including a 4-hour load bank test to verify exhaust system integrity and vibration levels.
h) Disposal of removed parts as per site waste management procedures.

6. COST IMPACT

7. SCHEDULE IMPACT

The required parts have a lead time of approximately 6–8 weeks from date of order confirmation.
Delivery will be to the Port of Lagos, followed by customs clearance and road transport to site

Total estimated schedule impact: **no impact on the overall maintenance outage window**, provided
the purchase order is raised by the date indicated above. If procurement is delayed beyond
15/08/2021, the installation will need to be deferred to the next planned maintenance window
(January 2022), as the generator cannot be taken offline outside the agreed outage schedule without
affecting plant availability guarantees.

8. JUSTIFICATION

The exhaust silencer on G-7 has developed visible corrosion and thinning at the lower shell section,
particularly around the drain point. Acoustic measurements taken on 12/07/2021 recorded a noise
level of 98 dB(A) at 1 metre from the silencer, against a design limit of 85 dB(A). The flexible
bellows show signs of fatigue cracking at the convolutions. Continued operation carries a risk of
exhaust leak, noise exceedance, and potential damage to the turbocharger outlet flange if the
bellows fail completely. Replacement is therefore recommended at the earliest opportunity.

approval authorises the procurement of the replacement exhaust silencer and flexible bellows, and

**12. SUPPLEMENTARY NOTE – REVISED INSTALLATION WINDOW**

Following the approval recorded in Section 9 above, the site maintenance team has reviewed the
proposed installation window against the current plant outage schedule. The originally indicated
window in Section 5 (dated 20/07/2021) is no longer fully available due to a delay in the
completion of the GT-2 combustion inspection, which has pushed the next planned outage start by
approximately two days. The revised installation window for the exhaust silencer and flexible
bellows replacement is now proposed as follows:

- **Proposed start:** 03/08/2021 (07:00 hours)
- **Proposed completion:** 05/08/2021 (18:00 hours)
- **Contingency allowance:** 1 day (to 06/08/2021) for unforeseen hold points

This revision does not alter the scope, cost, or schedule impact figures stated in Sections 6 and
7 of this Change Request. The cost impact remains as approved, and the schedule impact remains
within the originally approved outage duration of five (5) days. The revised window has been
coordinated with the plant operations team and is reflected in the updated outage plan issued
under reference OP-2021-071.

**13. CLARIFICATION – NOISE MEASUREMENT METHOD**

During the pre-approval technical review, a question was raised regarding the noise measurement
method used to identify the exhaust noise exceedance. For the avoidance of doubt, the measurement
referred to in Section 8 was taken in accordance with the plant's standard condition monitoring
procedure (CMP-012), using a handheld sound level meter set to 'A' weighting, slow response, at a
distance of 1 metre from the silencer casing, with the unit operating at base load. The measured
level was 93 dB(A), which exceeds the design limit of 85 dB(A). No further measurements have been
taken since the date of the original inspection. The replacement silencer specified in Appendix A
is expected to restore noise levels to within the design limit.

**14. CLARIFICATION – BELLOWS CONDITION AND REPLACEMENT SCOPE**

The flexible bellows assemblies identified in Section 5 are the inlet and outlet connections to
the exhaust silencer. The fatigue cracking observed at the convolutions is limited to the outlet
bellows; however, due to the common age and service history of both assemblies, and to avoid a
repeat outage in the near term, the scope includes replacement of both inlet and outlet bellows.
The inlet bellows will be replaced as a precautionary measure. No other exhaust path components
are included in this Change Request.

supersede or amend the approval recorded in Section 9. The original Change Request and this
supplement together constitute the full record of the approved change.
